title: The saints of Scripture kept God's commandments
source_text: X. Verum fideles per divinam gratiam posse Dei mandata servare omnium evidentissime probat ipsa experientia. Nam, Scriptura teste, multi sancti & pii homines de facto Dei mandata servarunt. Id de seipso David affirmare non veretur, Psal. 119. [marg.: Pausa Heth.] Festinavi, inquit, & non tardavi custodire mandata tua. Item, [marg.: Pausa Schin.] Custodivit anima mea testimonia tua: & dilexit ea vehementer. Servavi mandata tua & testimonia tua: quia omnes viae meae in conspectu tuo. Lucas autem Evangelista idem testimonium perhibet de Zacharia & Elizabeth illius uxore. Erant, inquit, justi ambo ante Deum, incedentes in omnibus mandatis & justificationibus Domini, sine querela. Quin omnes pii & fideles in scriptura frequenter describuntur per eos qui mandata Dei custodiunt: Ut quum dicit David psalmo modo citato, Socius ego sum omnium timentium te, & custodientium mandata tua.
pass_a_gloss: X. But that the faithful through divine grace can keep the commandments of God experience itself proves most evidently of all. For, Scripture being witness, many holy & godly men have in fact kept the commandments of God. David does not fear to affirm this of himself, Psal. 119. [margin: Pausa Heth] I hastened, he says, & did not delay to keep your commandments. Again, [margin: Pausa Schin] My soul has kept your testimonies: & has loved them exceedingly. I have kept your commandments & your testimonies: because all my ways are in your sight. And Luke the Evangelist bears the same witness of Zacharias & Elizabeth his wife. They were, he says, both righteous before God, walking in all the commandments & ordinances of the Lord, without complaint. Indeed all the godly & faithful are frequently described in scripture as those who keep the commandments of God: As when David says in the psalm just cited, I am a companion of all who fear you, & who keep your commandments.
pass_b_english: Thesis X. Experience itself proves most clearly of all that the faithful can keep God's commandments through God's grace, since Scripture testifies that many holy and devout people actually kept them. David does not hesitate to say so of himself in Psalm 119: 'I made haste and did not delay to keep your commandments' (margin: Pausa Heth); and again, 'My soul has kept your testimonies and loved them dearly. I have kept your commandments and your testimonies, for all my ways are before you' (margin: Pausa Schin).

Luke the Evangelist gives the same testimony of Zechariah and his wife Elizabeth: 'Both were righteous before God, walking blamelessly in all the commandments and ordinances of the Lord.' Indeed, Scripture often describes all the devout and faithful as those who keep God's commandments, as when David says in the same psalm, 'I am a companion of all who fear you and keep your commandments.'

lemmas.gloss: have in fact kept the commandments of God

choices.why: Scripture's phrase for the obedience of believers, kept distinct from perfect fulfilment of the law.
